raw.overview: All three advisors unanimously identify a critical conflict between the user's plan to sublease 40% of the 4,500 sq ft floor in Month 3 while retaining 60% occupancy for the full 36-month term and the lease's Clause 12.4, which grants the landlord an absolute, immediate recapture option upon any sublease notice. This clause directly threatens the constraint to maintain 60% occupancy throughout the entire term, as the landlord could terminate the entire lease rather than just the subleased portion, violating the core requirement.
raw.points_of_note: The advisors consistently cite Clause 12.4's unilateral recapture mechanism as the primary constraint violation, with Advisor 1 specifying the landlord's 'absolute, immediate recapture option,' Advisor 2 emphasizing the threat to 'entire Lease' termination, and Advisor 3 noting the 15-day window after any notice. All three confirm the lease's 36-month term and 4,500 sq ft total space align with the user's plan, but the recapture option's scope—applying to the whole lease rather than just the subleased 1,800 sq ft—creates an unresolvable conflict with the occupancy requirement.
raw.suggested_next_step: Conduct a focused review of Clause 12.4 to determine if the landlord's recapture right can be contractually modified, waived, or limited to the subleased portion only, ensuring the 60% occupancy remains secure for the full 36-month term.

consensus.text:
ASSESSMENT OVERVIEW: All three advisors unanimously identify a critical conflict between the user's plan to sublease 40% of the 4,500 sq ft floor in Month 3 while retaining 60% occupancy for the full 36-month term and the lease's Clause 12.4, which grants the landlord an absolute, immediate recapture option upon any sublease notice. This clause directly threatens the constraint to maintain 60% occupancy throughout the entire term, as the landlord could terminate the entire lease rather than just the subleased portion, violating the core requirement.
POINTS OF NOTE: The advisors consistently cite Clause 12.4's unilateral recapture mechanism as the primary constraint violation, with Advisor 1 specifying the landlord's 'absolute, immediate recapture option,' Advisor 2 emphasizing the threat to 'entire Lease' termination, and Advisor 3 noting the 15-day window after any notice. All three confirm the lease's 36-month term and 4,500 sq ft total space align with the user's plan, but the recapture option's scope—applying to the whole lease rather than just the subleased 1,800 sq ft—creates an unresolvable conflict with the occupancy requirement.
SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: Conduct a focused review of Clause 12.4 to determine if the landlord's recapture right can be contractually modified, waived, or limited to the subleased portion only, ensuring the 60% occupancy remains secure for the full 36-month term.
